About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Team

Ramp builds software that moves real money — corporate cards, bill payments, reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running, and our CX team is the frontline when something needs to be resolved fast.

Premier Support is the dedicated support team for Ramp's largest and most complex customers - the Enterprise and Strategic accounts running global, multi-entity finance operations on Ramp. Our specialists support these accounts with real depth: they know the businesses, stakeholders, and systems, and they're the people the customer comes to when something matters. It's high-touch, relationship-led support.

About the Role

Ramp is hiring an Associate Manager to lead Premier Support. This is a small team of senior specialists - six today, scaling meaningfully, who are the daily point of contact for the accounts Ramp can least afford to get wrong.

You'll own the people and the performance. That means coaching specialists who operate with real autonomy, hold a high bar for quality and responsiveness when the stakes are high, and are the person your team escalates to when an account is experiencing challenges. You'll partner daily with the Account Managers who own the strategy for these same accounts - they own the account direction, you own the support experience that makes it possible.

This team is new. The playbook exists but it isn't finished, and you'll be shaping it. That means you need to be someone who can build and lead at the same time: designing the operating rhythm, spotting where the model breaks before it breaks, and having a contingency ready when something doesn't land. You'll be trusted with a lot early, and you'll have a manager who has built these teams from scratch and stays close.

This is a people-leadership job first. We're looking for someone genuinely passionate about managing people and building strong, solid teams. Someone who finds the craft of leadership itself interesting, not just the outcomes it produces.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and develop a team of senior specialists. Run weekly 1:1s, give feedback that changes behavior, and build development plans that grow real ownership and judgment. Know your people well enough to make coaching specific.

  • Own performance directly. Set a clear bar, recognize and grow your strongest people, and address gaps early and honestly. You'll have the hard conversations yourself, with a plan and a follow-through.

  • Own your team's results. Quality, responsiveness, and SLA delivery across the accounts your team supports - plus the day-to-day mechanics that get you there: triage by account risk, load balancing, coverage, and on-call rotation.

  • Own escalations. Be the point of accountability when a strategic account escalates - driving it to resolution, keeping partners informed, and making sure it gets raised cleanly to Product or Engineering when it needs to.

  • Partner with Account Management. Work shoulder-to-shoulder on shared accounts: surfacing risk, feeding product and account signals back, and making Premier a partner they rely on.

  • Use data to decide. Read the quality, SLA, escalation, and volume trends; find the root cause; turn it into coaching or a process change.

  • Build what's missing. Turn recurring patterns from your accounts into durable playbooks, documentation, and processes. Manage capacity as the book grows, so quality scales faster than headcount.

  • Work with AI tools daily. Ramp is actively building AI into CX operations. You'll adopt and champion AI-powered workflows, help your team get fluent, and shape how these tools evolve. Comfort with new technology isn't optional - we are all builders at Ramp.

  • Lead through change. Premier will look different in six months. You'll make that feel manageable for your team, and you'll anticipate the next change before it arrives.

What You Need

  • Minimum 2 years of people-management experience - direct accountability for others' performance, development, and difficult conversations

  • Minimum 4 years in customer-facing support, technical account management, or customer success, including experience with enterprise or complex B2B accounts

  • Demonstrated ability to manage performance honestly and effectively - you can point to a time you turned someone around, and a time you concluded you couldn't

  • Proven experience leading a team through significant change - a reorg, a new operating model, a tooling migration and evidence of how you kept the team steady

  • Strong analytical instincts - you work from data, find root causes, and can defend a decision with evidence

  • Excellent written and verbal communication - you can be crisp with executives, clear with your team, and calm with an escalating customer

  • Comfort leading in ambiguity, where you're building the process while running it

  • Experience using AI tools to improve support or account workflows - research, drafting, process automation

  • Availability to flex outside standard hours when accounts require it, including a weekend on-call rotation and occasional holiday coverage

What would make you stand out

  • You've managed a named book of B2B accounts or led a team that did, and you understand the difference between closing a ticket and protecting a relationship

  • You've built something: an AI-powered workflow, an automation, a reporting layer your team actually uses. Not "I used AI to analyze data" but "I found a gap, figured out how to close it, and shipped it."

  • You've stood up a team or function from an early stage, and you know what breaks at 6 people versus 15

  • You've partnered closely with Customer Success, Account Management, or Sales, and can speak to how you handled the tension when priorities diverged

  • Background in FinTech or financial services; comfort with ERP and accounting systems (NetSuite, Workday, Sage Intacct)

  • You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code

  • Experience in a premium, dedicated, or VIP support model at a high-growth company

For candidates located in NYC or SF, the pay range for this role is $108,000 - $132,000. For candidates located in all other locations, the pay range for this role is $100,000 - $125,000.

Be the point of accountability when a strategic account escalates - driving it to resolution, keeping partners informed, and making sure it gets raised cleanly to Product or Engineering when it needs to. - Partner with Account Management. Work shoulder-to-shoulder on shared accounts: surfacing risk, feeding product and account signals back, and making Premier a partner they rely on. - Use data to decide. Read the quality, SLA, escalation, and volume trends; find the root cause; turn it into coaching or a process change. - Build what's missing. Turn recurring patterns from your accounts into durable playbooks, documentation, and processes. Manage capacity as the book grows, so quality scales faster than headcount. - Work with AI tools daily. Ramp is actively building AI into CX operations. You'll adopt and champion AI-powered workflows, help your team get fluent, and shape how these tools evolve. Comfort with new technology isn't optional - we are all builders at Ramp. - Lead through change. Premier will look different in six months. You'll make that feel manageable for your team, and you'll anticipate the next change before it arrives. About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Technical Consultants are on the frontlines working to establish partnerships with Ramp customers, and act as a liaison between customers and our internal technical teams. You'll be partnering with Customer Activation & Account Management teams to identify, prioritize and build financial solutions for new and existing customers so that Ramp continues to scale with their needs.

You will act as the technical and financial subject matter expert for our customers and design solutions that address the customer's needs through Ramp and partner integrations. You will partner with Post-Sales teams to drive Product, Design and Engineering teams' roadmaps to evolve Ramp to better serve our customers at scale and offer increasingly higher value.

You will define the customer's financial & technical success criteria from onboarding through activation and expansion. You will represent Product, Design, and Engineering externally and will operate with deep conviction and understanding of Ramp's technical capabilities. The role requires technical skills necessary to understand and educate on robust accounting features and integrate them across all the touchpoints and surface area of a customer.

This role is specifically focused on Enterprise customers running Oracle Fusion Cloud, supporting large, complex organizations with multi-entity environments, advanced ERP integrations, and highly customized financial workflows.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as the primary Technical Consultant for Enterprise accounts running Oracle Cloud, supporting complex, high-impact customers with multi-entity, multi-ERP, and global financial environments

  • Act as a technical advisor to customers and Ramp's internal teams while supporting high-value implementations and expansion opportunities by guiding Oracle Cloud integration, configuration, and system design

  • Partner with Customer Activation and Account Management teams to assess customer requirements and propose scalable solutions involving Oracle Cloud, HRIS, and API integrations

  • Collaborate with onboarding specialists and implementation leads to support technical workstreams, ensuring faster time-to-value and customer success

  • Work with customers to problem-solve technical hurdles and propose effective product implementations with a deep understanding of Oracle Cloud integration and configuration options

  • Participate in technical discovery to understand customer Oracle Cloud environments and workflows, and recommend best-fit Ramp architecture including when and how to use Ramp's API

  • Be a subject matter expert across Oracle Cloud and Ramp's accounting integration capabilities, partnering with Sales, Product and partners to advocate for integration development aligned with customer needs

  • Troubleshoot Oracle Cloud integration blockers and guide customers through complex configuration decisions

  • Contribute to internal documentation and tooling that scales Ramp's ability to support Oracle Cloud integration use cases across a growing customer base

  • Influence Ramp's product roadmap by channeling Oracle Cloud customer pain points and feedback to the Product and Engineering teams

What You Need

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, finance, business, or a related field

  • 4+ years in technical consulting, solutions engineering, implementation, or a similar customer-facing technical role, ideally in a SaaS or fintech environment

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience working with Oracle Fusion Cloud, including financials modules, integration patterns, and enterprise deployment models

  • Deep familiarity with Oracle Cloud Financials accounting workflows, including core functionalities involving General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Subledger Accounting, and multi-org structures

  • Comfort working with APIs, integration logic, and system architecture and being able to explain those concepts to finance and operations stakeholders

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Design on enterprise-driven gaps, influencing roadmap decisions that unlock scale across Ramp's largest customers

  • Advise on non-standard Oracle Cloud implementations and edge cases, balancing customer needs with long-term platform scalability and supportability

  • Strong communication skills: able to translate complex technical solutions into business value and guide customers toward scalable approaches

  • Collaborative mindset and ability to work cross-functionally with Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering

  • Exceptional organization and problem-solving skills, with a bias toward action and a high level of ownership

  • Thrives in ambiguity and fast-paced environments; adaptable and resourceful as we scale Ramp's upmarket motion

Nice to Have

  • Oracle Cloud Procurement and/or Oracle Projects (PPM) implementation experience

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

  • Evidence of helping individuals and/or peers improve performance and progress in their careers.

  • Strong written and verbal communication

  • Self-starter with a high sense of urgency

  • Strong ability to prioritize and multitask

  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment

  • Ability to work 5x a week in office, in London, United Kingdom

Nice-to-Haves

  • Fluency in additional European languages

  • Experience leading BDR teams with a proven track record of exceeding goal

  • Experience in a high-growth startup, consulting, VC, IB/PE, or other analytically intensive environments

  • Previous experience in a customer-facing role, ideally within a fast-paced environment

  • Prior CRM experience (preferably Salesforce)

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Please note that this role will require you to be comfortable with working in-person at our NYC or SF office 3 days/week. We will sponsor you for relocation if you need to move for this role.

What You’ll Do

  • Drive the scheduling process and communicate logistics to all candidates and hiring teams

  • Build a world-class team by providing a high-touch “white glove” experience at every step of the interview process

  • Act as the primary contact during virtual and in-person interviews

  • Develop collaborative relationships with Talent team members, hiring managers, and interviewers

  • Spot and flag what isn't working such as interviewer load imbalances, bottlenecked stages, slow feedback and bring fixes

  • Manage workflows within GSuite, Ramp’s ATS (Ashby), and scheduling tools for automation

What You’ll Need

  • 0-1+ years of coordination / admin experience, ideally in start-up or high-growth environments

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to quickly build trust and rapport

  • Organizational and time-management skills with superb attention to detail

  • Comfort working at high volume and re-prioritizing mid-day when plans change, interviews get moved, interviewers cancel, and you'll need to solve it without dropping anything else

  • A bias toward urgency: you respond quickly and follow through without being chased

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with Ashby and Modernloop (or other ATS / scheduling tools)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp wins when our customers win. Ramp’s customer base is scaling rapidly, spanning more businesses, more users, and more use cases across increasingly complex finance operations. At the same time, our expanding product surface area — from cards and expense management to bill payments, procurement, vendor management, accounting automation, and emerging products — is creating more nuanced customer needs and more cross-functional support moments. AI is changing what is possible in parallel: giving CX new ways to route, resolve, and guide customers, while raising the bar for where human judgment, specialization, and consultative support matter most.

We are hiring a Director to lead a critical part of our omni-channel Customer Experience organization: the teams and leaders serving customers across Phone, Email, and Chat. You will lead within a 24/7 customer operation, ensuring the right coverage, leadership, and customer experience across channels. This role is accountable for the performance of its channel portfolio, helping customers get the right answer quickly and delivering consistent results across quality, speed, productivity, and customer satisfaction.

The role combines direct leadership of channel teams with close partnership across CX Operations, CX Specialized teams, CX AI Ops, and Product Operations. You will develop strong managers and frontline teams, create real accountability, and stay close enough to the work to understand where customers and teams are getting stuck. You will translate the department’s direction into clear priorities, stronger operating routines, and measurable improvements across Phone, Email, and Chat.

Because Ramp’s CX team sits within the Product organization, this role has close ties to the technical teams and products our customers use every day. That proximity gives CX a unique opportunity to turn frontline insight into better workflows, stronger product feedback loops, and an AI-powered way of working.

This role is a strong fit for a thoughtful, hands-on leader who learns quickly, raises the bar, and makes clear decisions in a fast-changing environment. You are comfortable owning the day-to-day, rolling up your sleeves to understand the work and the product deeply, developing people, setting high standards, and turning complex problems into clear plans that improve outcomes for customers and teams. You will help define how managers lead, how frontline teams use AI and automation, where human judgment matters most, how channels work together, and how CX scales through Ramp’s next chapter.

If you love building high-performing teams, solving hard operational problems, and helping customers win through rapid product, business, and AI-driven change, this role is for you.

What You’ll Do

  • Own day-to-day channel execution — lead Phone, Email, and Chat teams, stay close to the work, and drive frontline performance across customer satisfaction, quality, service levels, resolution quality, and productivity.

  • Develop CX leadership — coach Managers, set clear expectations, and build accountability for team performance and customer outcomes.

  • Serve as an escalation point — help resolve high-priority customer and internal escalations, bringing sound judgment, urgency, and clear communication to complex issues.

  • Improve tools, workflows, and channel execution — use product knowledge, customer feedback, quality findings, and performance data to improve operating routines, resolve cross-channel trade-offs, and partner with CX Operations, CX Specialized teams, AI, Product Operations, Product, Engineering, Risk, and other stakeholders on better workflows and automation opportunities.

  • Challenge how we operate — evaluate whether our metrics, workflows, team structures, training, and operating model meet today’s customer and business needs. Bring a founder mindset by questioning assumptions, testing new approaches, and helping the organization evolve.

  • Shape the AI-powered future of CX — define how CX should evolve as Ramp grows, including how managers lead, how frontline teams use AI and automation, where specialization improves the customer experience, and where human judgment should be elevated.

  • Turn strategy and emerging opportunities into scalable operations — translate department priorities and new business areas into clear channel plans, repeatable processes, strong change management, and high adoption across Phone, Email, and Chat.

What You Need

  • Experience as a leader who has managed large, complex operational teams in a fast-paced environment; traditional support experience is valuable but not required.

  • Exceptional learning agility and horsepower, with startup or similarly high-ownership operating experience; you learn new domains quickly, move through ambiguity, and build structure without waiting for perfect information.

  • A record of improving customer-facing operations through rigorous analysis, strategic problem solving, and strong execution, including finding practical solutions to complex problems others may miss.

  • An empathetic, direct leadership style that develops people while holding a high personal and team bar for performance, quality, ownership, and follow-through.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to align teams and cross-functional partners around difficult decisions.

  • A builder mentality around technology and operations, with experience using AI, automation, or workflow tooling to transform the customer and team experience and drive changes from idea to adoption.

  • Curiosity about the business behind the support motion, with the ability to connect customer needs, product complexity, frontline workflows, and company priorities.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience leading multiple customer-facing channels, such as Phone, Email, Chat, or other real-time and asynchronous support operations.

  • Experience in FinTech, financial services, or another complex, highly regulated environment.

  • Experience partnering with operations, product, or tooling teams to improve customer-facing workflows across multiple teams.

  • Experience scaling customer operations at a high-growth startup.

Compensation

For candidates located in New York City or San Francisco, the base salary range for this role is $220,000–$290,000. For candidates located in all other locations, the base salary range will be between $190,000-$260,000.

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

About the Role

We’re looking for an IT Site Specialist to join our IT Team at Ramp based in our San Francisco office! This is a temporary full-time on-site role that blends hands-on, in-person site support with ownership of our core SaaS application stack, and we weigh both sides equally. On the site side, you’ll be the primary IT presence in SF — owning deskside support, onboarding/offboarding, endpoint and AV support, and office inventory. On the application side, you’ll administer the tools the whole company depends on — Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, JAMF, and a growing set of SaaS platforms — owning provisioning, access, portfolio, renewals, integrations, and automation. We’re looking for someone who takes pride in running a smooth on-the-ground operation while also thinking like a systems owner who scales IT through automation and sound identity practices.

What You’ll Do

  • Provide in-person support at our San Francisco office 5 days/week, acting as the site’s primary IT point of contact.

  • Perform IT Support Specialist (L4) duties, encompassing all responsibilities of the IT Support Specialist role.

  • Provide deskside/walk-up support and resolve IT tickets end-to-end.

  • Handle advanced troubleshooting and internal escalation before handoff to Pod 2 – IT Engineering.

  • Triage and field support requests across tickets, email, Slack, and the team-it-ops and help-it distros; proactively work to minimize volume and improve SLAs.

  • Direct and review Serval (AI support agent) workflow runs — step in when automated resolution fails, and contribute workflow builds and guidance improvements.

  • Coordinate application onboarding/offboarding tied to lifecycle events (joiner/mover/leaver) — provisioning, deprovisioning, and access changes across the SaaS stack.

  • Administer core applications (Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, JAMF, and other SaaS tools): user lifecycle, group/role management, and SSO/SCIM integrations.

  • Own application portfolio management — seat counts, usage tracking, and license optimization.

  • Manage SaaS renewals — tracking contract dates and coordinating renewals/cancellations.

  • Partner with Pod 3 on SaaS App Strategy execution from an operational/usage standpoint.

  • Build and maintain integrations and automations to reduce manual work and enforce least-privilege access.

  • Manage on-site hardware inventory, lifecycle, and procurement coordination — stock levels, reorder requests, and coordinating with fulfillment vendors (e.g., Firstbase, SHI, CDW, Amazon).

  • Support AV/conference room reliability in the SF office.

  • Take ownership of small and large projects, partnering with internal and external teams to deliver.

  • Perform recurring audits on application licenses, access, and hardware; drive remediation.

  • Create technical and user-facing documentation; push the team toward industry best practices.

  • Be an advocate for our users — understand their challenges and remove blockers with empathy.

What You Need

  • Minimum 4 years of technical experience in an enterprise-size organization, with hands-on experience in both on-site IT support and SaaS/application administration.

  • Strong knowledge of our core tech stack: Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, JAMF, and modern SaaS tools.

  • Solid understanding of User Lifecycle Management, identity/access management, and least-privilege principles.

  • Experience with SSO/SCIM provisioning and building integrations or automations across SaaS platforms.

  • Experience managing SaaS application portfolios, license optimization, and vendor renewals.

  • Experience with deskside support, ticket resolution, and knowing when to escalate to an engineering team.

  • Comfort owning the physical site experience — endpoint troubleshooting, AV, and inventory — alongside back-end application administration.

  • Strong attention to detail, execution-oriented, and comfortable owning ambiguous, cross-functional work.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience in high-growth startups.

  • Experience managing macOS/Windows in hybrid/remote environments.

  • Scripting/automation experience (e.g., Python, API integrations, workflow tools).

  • Experience with AI-assisted support tooling and workflow automation (e.g., Serval or similar).

  • Experience coordinating hardware procurement with fulfillment vendors (e.g., Firstbase, SHI, CDW).

  • Okta Certified Professional / Administrator.

  • Slack Certified Admin.

  • Google Workspace Administrator experience.

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is known for insane product velocity, sitting at the center of AI and finance, and saving customers meaningful amounts of time and money. Increasingly, companies come to us to understand how the best finance teams are actually operating, whether that’s our own team or the customers we serve.

Right now, those conversations happen behind closed doors and Zoom windows. We want to pull them out, write them down, and make them useful to more people. We’re hiring a Finance Storytelling Lead to do exactly that.

You will spend roughly half your time embedded with Ramp’s Finance team, learning what it means to run an AI-pilled finance team at a company building AI solutions for finance. The other half of your time will support customer storytelling with the finance customer in mind, working closely with Brand Communications, Sales, and Customer Marketing.

For both, you’ll pull out the useful lessons and turn them into stories people want to learn from, whether that means writing in your own voice or for our CFO and Finance leadership team, shaping a customer story, or finding the right external conversation for Ramp to join. How these stories come to life is up to you. Social content, videos, earned media, exec bylines – there are many ways this can go.

The primary skill set is you have a journalist’s instincts. You can sit through a messy meeting, spot the thing that matters, ask the question no one else asked, and turn it into a piece of work with a point of view.

At the end of the day, you’ll play a large role in making Ramp the company finance leaders want to learn from, not just buy from.

 

What You'll Do

  • Find the story in the work. Embed with Ramp Finance and gain the trust needed to see how the team actually operates. Turn planning meetings, closes, decisions, experiments, and customer conversations into ideas worth sharing with the wider finance world.

  • Spend a large portion of your time writing. Develop first-person posts, points of view, customer stories, and other formats to be determined.

  • Create original finance insights. Work with Ramp’s Finance team, customers, and Economics Lab to identify questions our data cannot answer. Then take that and turn CFO and finance-leader patterns into original research, surveys, practitioner-led analysis, and points of view that Ramp can own.

  • Build the finance-storytelling system. Create a repeatable way to identify ideas, capture the raw material, develop drafts, and ship. Finance should not need to become a content team for Ramp to publish what it knows.

  • Ramp's Proprietary Spend Data. Collaborate closely with the data and economics team to identify trends in the Ramp Spend Dataset that lead or support storytelling around trends in Business's finance stack and spend.

  • Make customer stories do more. Partner with Customer Marketing, Sales, and Communications to find customers whose finance teams have something real to teach and help them teach it.

  • Own the distribution engine. Build the audience plan for each piece: who needs to see it, where they already spend time, which voice should carry it, and how we know it worked.

  • Set the bar for finance content. Decide what earns a finance leader’s attention and what does not.

 

What You Need

  • You are an exceptional writer. You can make complicated financial or operational ideas clear without making them bland. You have strong reporting instincts and an opinion about structure.

  • You understand finance. Ideally, you have covered or worked closely with CFOs, accounting, FP&A, corporate finance, treasury, payments, capital allocation, or the businesses that sell to finance teams. You know enough to ask good questions, hear the difference between a real insight and a polished answer, and keep learning.

  • You are data literate. You can use AI and trusted data to explore a question, find a sharp metric, and turn it into a story or headline-making chart.

  • You can write in someone else’s voice. You know the difference between writing about an executive and writing as one. You can preserve a leader’s point of view, rhythm, and convictions while making the work sharper.

  • You move without a perfect brief. You can take rough notes and turn them into something strong.

  • You are AI-native, but use personal judgement. You use AI to reduce busywork, explore angles, and move faster. But you don’t offload your brain to an LLM.

  • You are based in New York City and want to work closely with a team in person. If you aren’t in NYC right now, we’ll cover your relocation.

 

Fair Warning

  • This role is not for someone who prefers an established playbook.

  • It's not for someone who needs to be methodical before being experimental. We experiment first and systematize what works.

  • It’s not for a senior adviser who prefers to give direction versus do. This is a true Super IC role.

  • It's not for someone who finds comfort in a predictable pace. The pace here is genuinely uncomfortable. The right person finds that fun.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Technical Consultants are on the frontlines working to establish partnerships with Ramp customers, and act as a liaison between customers and our internal technical teams. You'll be partnering with Customer Activation & Account Management teams to identify, prioritize and build financial solutions for new and existing customers so that Ramp continues to scale with their needs.

You will act as the technical and financial subject matter expert for our customers and design solutions that address the customer's needs through Ramp and partner integrations. You will partner with Post-Sales teams to drive Product, Design and Engineering teams' roadmaps to evolve Ramp to better serve our customers at scale and offer increasingly higher value.

You will define the customer's financial & technical success criteria from onboarding through activation and expansion. You will represent Product, Design, and Engineering externally and will operate with deep conviction and understanding of Ramp's technical capabilities. The role requires technical skills necessary to understand and educate on robust accounting features and integrate them across all the touchpoints and surface area of a customer.

This role is specifically focused on Enterprise customers running Microsoft F&O, supporting large, complex organizations with multi-entity environments, advanced ERP integrations, and highly customized financial workflows.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as the primary Technical Consultant for Enterprise accounts running Microsoft F&O , supporting complex, high-impact customers with multi-entity, multi-ERP, and global financial environments

  • Act as a technical advisor to customers and Ramp's internal teams while supporting high-value implementations and expansion opportunities by guiding Microsoft F&O integration, configuration, and system design

  • Partner with Customer Activation and Account Management teams to assess customer requirements and propose scalable solutions involving F&O, HRIS, and API integrations

  • Collaborate with onboarding specialists and implementation leads to support technical workstreams, ensuring faster time-to-value and customer success

  • Work with customers to problem-solve technical hurdles and propose effective product implementations with a deep understanding of Dynamics F&O integration and configuration options

  • Participate in technical discovery to understand customer F&O environments and workflows, and recommend best-fit Ramp architecture including when and how to use Ramp's API

  • Be a subject matter expert across F&O and Ramp's accounting integration capabilities, partnering with Sales, Product and partners to advocate for integration development aligned with customer needs

  • Troubleshoot Dynamics F&O integration blockers and guide customers through complex configuration decisions

  • Contribute to internal documentation and tooling that scales Ramp's ability to support F&O integration use cases across a growing customer base

  • Influence Ramp's product roadmap by channeling F&O customer pain points and feedback to the Product and Engineering teams

What You Need

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, finance, business, or a related field

  • 4+ years in technical consulting, solutions engineering, implementation, or a similar customer-facing technical role, ideally in a SaaS or fintech environment

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience working with Microsoft Dynamics F&O, including financials modules, integration patterns, and enterprise deployment models

  • Deep familiarity with accounting workflows, including core functionalities involving General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Subledger Accounting, and multi-org structures

  • Comfort working with APIs, integration logic, and system architecture and being able to explain those concepts to finance and operations stakeholders

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Design on enterprise-driven gaps, influencing roadmap decisions that unlock scale across Ramp's largest customers

  • Advise on non-standard F&O implementations and edge cases, balancing customer needs with long-term platform scalability and supportability

  • Strong communication skills: able to translate complex technical solutions into business value and guide customers toward scalable approaches

  • Collaborative mindset and ability to work cross-functionally with Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering

  • Exceptional organization and problem-solving skills, with a bias toward action and a high level of ownership

  • Thrives in ambiguity and fast-paced environments; adaptable and resourceful as we scale Ramp's upmarket motion

About the Role

As a Product Manager at Ramp, you will be responsible for the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Ramp’s international payments products. You will lead a core team of engineers and designers to build and scale global money movement capabilities that enable our customers to pay vendors, employees, and partners around the world. You’ll own a critical set of customer and business problems at the intersection of payments, compliance, risk, and FX — driving end-to-end product vision, strategy, and execution to power Ramp’s global expansion and meet ambitious company goals. Your scope will include:

  1. Cross-border payments & FX – Own the experience and infrastructure for sending and receiving international payments across currencies and geographies, including FX pricing, rate transparency, settlement speed, and reliability across multiple payment rails.

  2. Global partner ecosystem – Evaluate, integrate, and manage banking, FX, and local payment service partners to expand Ramp’s coverage, improve unit economics, and unlock new corridors and capabilities.

  3. Compliance & risk infrastructure – Partner with Legal, Compliance, and Risk to design scalable KYC/KYB, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, and regulatory frameworks that enable safe and compliant international money movement.

  4. New market expansion – Launch international capabilities in new geographies, navigating local regulations, licensing requirements, and operational constraints while delivering a seamless customer experience.

We’re looking for someone who can partner and collaborate across various internal teams, has a deep understanding of our customers and technology, and can deliver financial products to streamline complex business flows via a fantastic user experience.

What You'll Do

  • Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for international payments at Ramp

  • Drive high-velocity execution with a world-class team of engineers and designers, balancing principled intuition with data-driven decision making

  • Marry customer insights with technical possibilities, crafting intuitive user experiences that abstract away complexity

  • Help thousands of finance teams on Ramp more successfully manage their finances by expanding the capabilities of our product

  • Prototype rapidly using tools like Claude to accelerate the product development lifecycle and fast-forward to production-ready products.

  • Stay deeply plugged into AI research, industry trends, and emergent applications, filtering signal from noise and applying it creatively to Ramp’s product

What You Need

  • BA/BS in a technical or analytical field

  • Minimum 3 years product management experience

  • Strong customer empathy and design thinking

  • Fluency in data and how to make data-driven product decisions

  • Experience evaluating product decisions and prioritization trade-offs

  • Demonstrated ability to lead and influence small teams of engineers & designers toward a common goal

  • Ability to collaborate with multiple stakeholders and large cross-functional teams

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Passion for AI, shown through hands-on building, prototyping, or side projects, and staying current on research and tools.

  • Fluency with modern prototyping tools (e.g. Cursor, Bolt, Claude Code) and comfort with design/collaboration environments like Figma and Git.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Background in fast-paced, high-growth startup environments

  • Experience building payments products or products in regulated markets

  • Experience building products with a significant AI component, especially if leveraging LLMs.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the role

As the founding Channel Partner Manager for Canada, you will build the partner motion that helps Canadian businesses discover, evaluate, and adopt Ramp through trusted advisors and ecosystem partners.

This is a zero-to-one role. You will own the full partner lifecycle, from identifying and engaging Canadian accounting, advisory, private equity, and venture capital partners through signing, enablement, activation, and partner-sourced pipeline. Your early results will help determine how Ramp scales its Canadian channel motion.

You will work closely with Sales, Growth, Product, Engineering, and the broader Partnerships organization. The right person is a hands-on builder: equally comfortable opening a new relationship, running a partner meeting, solving an operational blocker, and turning early learnings into a repeatable playbook.

What you’ll do

  • Build Ramp’s Canadian channel strategy and operating rhythm from the ground up.

  • Research, identify, source, qualify and sign net-new Canadian partners.

  • Create joint go-to-market and activation plans to grow the Canadian partner ecosystem.

  • Drive revenue for Ramp through generating referrals

  • Develop trusted relationships with decision-makers and operators inside partner orgs

  • Educate partners on Ramp’s Canadian capabilities, value prop and updates.

  • Own partner onboarding, activation, pipeline generation, and regular business reviews.

  • Work closely with the Canadian Sales team to advance partner-referred opportunities.

  • Partner with Product to surface recurring partner needs and inform the Canadian roadmap.

What you’ll need

  • 5+ years of relevant experience, including 3+ years in partner sales, business development, channel partnerships, or a closely related role

  • High agency, urgency, and resilience

  • Proven track record of sourcing and managing partnerships

  • Self-starter mindset: you are comfortable getting in the weeds

  • Strong discovery and consultative-selling skills

  • Excellent written and verbal communication

  • Strong operating discipline and comfort using data to improve performance.

  • Proven ability to succeed in a fast-paced environment

  • Strong cross-functional judgment and a history of finding success across cross-functional work

  • Familiarity with the Canadian business and technology ecosystem

  • Strong comfort using AI tools to execute quality work, fast

Nice to have

  • Experience building a new partner motion, market, or vertical from an early stage.

  • Professional proficiency or native-level fluency in French

  • Presence in the Canadian accounting, advisory, private equity, venture capital, financial-services, or technology partner network

  • Familiarity with finance & accounting workflows and solutions

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Technical Consulting is Ramp's post-sales technical delivery team. When a finance org needs Ramp to work the way their business actually runs, this is the team that takes customers through that transformation, from complex accounting issues to integration errors to everything in between.

The Senior Manager, Technical Consulting, Strategic leads the team responsible for Ramp's largest and most strategic accounts. You'll own post-sales technical implementation for this segment end to end — from technical discovery and solution design through go-live, adoption, and expansion — working shoulder-to-shoulder with our Customer Activation team, with whom you'll co-own activation milestones and time-to-value.

Strategic customers arrive with multi-entity structures, legacy ERPs, in-flight finance transformations, procurement and treasury requirements, and executive sponsors who expect a named technical leader in the room. Your team is the last line of technical escalation for these accounts — there is no tier above you.

This role suits an experienced leader who can hold two things at once: the operating rigor to run a delivery function at scale, and the technical credibility to sit across from a Controller or VP of Finance and design the solution live.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and grow the Strategic Technical Consulting team — coach senior and principal-level consultants, own hiring, onboarding, performance, and career architecture, and build a bench deep enough to scale with the segment

  • Own post-sales technical implementation for Ramp's largest accounts — accountable for solution quality, delivery timelines, and technical outcomes across the portfolio

  • Co-own activation milestones with Customer Activation — build a joint operating model where TC drives technical design and Activation drives adoption and enablement, with shared accountability for time-to-value and a single, coherent customer experience

  • Serve as the terminal escalation point for complex technical and delivery challenges — ERP integration failures, custom API work, at-risk go-lives, and commitments made pre-sales that need to be re-scoped

  • Define the Strategic delivery model — scoping standards, solution design review, rules of engagement with CSM/AM/Activation, staffing and capacity models, and quality bars that hold up under enterprise scrutiny

  • Run the function with operational rigor — forecast capacity, balance workload across accounts, instrument the team with KPIs (time-to-value, go-live on-time rate, escalation volume, adoption and expansion attach), and use the data in coaching and planning

  • Partner cross-functionally at the leadership level — Customer Activation, Strategic CSM and AM, Sales, Product, Engineering, and GTM Ops — to align on roadmap, feedback loops, and segment strategy

  • Turn field insight into product influence — synthesize what Strategic customers actually need, champion it with Product and Engineering, and close the loop back to the field

  • Set precedent where none exists — make sound calls in ambiguous, high-stakes situations, document the reasoning, and teach the team to do the same

What You Need

  • 8+ years in technical consulting, solutions architecture, implementation, or professional services — with substantial time on enterprise or strategic accounts

  • 3+ years managing individual contributors and owning team-level outcomes; experience managing senior or principal-level ICs strongly preferred

  • Proven track record owning post-sales implementation for large, complex customers — multi-entity, multi-system, executive-sponsored engagements

  • Deep fluency in ERP and financial systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Oracle, Workday Financials, Microsoft Dynamics), APIs, SSO/HRIS integrations, and core accounting workflows (chart of accounts, subsidiaries, approval hierarchies, month-end close)

  • Ability to assess and guide technical solution design at enterprise complexity — and to tell the difference between a configuration problem, a product gap, and a customer process problem

  • Experience building the operating model between two functions — e.g. delivery and onboarding, or services and customer success — and making shared accountability actually work

  • Executive-grade communication — able to hold the room with a CFO or Controller, advocate for your team internally, and translate technical trade-offs into business consequences

  • Demonstrated judgment in ambiguity and a bias toward ownership in a fast-changing, high-growth environment

Nice to Have

  • Experience at an ERP or financial systems vendor (Workday, NetSuite/Oracle, Sage Intacct, Coupa) or in a Big 4 / systems integrator implementation practice

  • Background in fintech, spend management, or AP automation

  • Experience standing up or scaling a technical consulting / professional services function from an early stage

  • Experience managing managers or team leads, or building the career ladder for a technical IC track

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Emerging Talent is an important part of how Ramp builds for the long term. It gives us the opportunity to meet exceptional people early, build relationships before they enter the broader talent market, and develop the next generation of Ramp talent.

We’re hiring a Recruiter to help build and execute our Emerging Talent programs. You’ll own full-cycle recruiting across early-career roles and internships, partnering closely with hiring teams to identify, assess, and close exceptional candidates.

A big part of the job is finding talent before everyone else does. You’ll build relationships with students and early-career candidates, develop new ways to reach high-potential talent, and help create an exceptional experience from a candidate’s first interaction with Ramp through offer and, for our interns, potential conversion to full-time. You’ll also have the opportunity to improve how we operate, test new approaches, and help shape a growing Emerging Talent function.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own full-cycle recruiting across Ramp’s Emerging Talent roles

  • Partner with hiring managers across Engineering, Product, and other teams to define hiring needs, align on candidate profiles, and calibrate on early-career talent

  • Identify and engage high-potential candidates through universities, student communities, technical networks, referrals, events, and other emerging-talent channels

  • Lead offer and closing processes, building strong candidate relationships and helping exceptional talent understand the opportunity to build their careers at Ramp

  • Support the execution of Ramp’s internship programs, including candidate programming, events, intern engagement, and intern-to-full-time conversion

  • Use recruiting data to understand pipeline health, identify opportunities, and keep hiring teams informed on progress and outcomes

  • Create an exceptional candidate experience that is thoughtful, transparent, and high-touch at every stage

  • Experiment with new ways to identify, engage, and hire exceptional talent early, and help turn what works into repeatable recruiting practices

 

What You Need

  • 5+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience; experience with Emerging Talent, university, campus, or early-career recruiting is a plus

  • A track record of identifying and engaging exceptional talent, with strong instincts for candidate quality

  • The ability to quickly learn new talent markets, calibrate to a high hiring bar, and recruit across different roles and functions

  • Strong operational rigor and the ability to manage high-volume pipelines, competing priorities, and frequent context changes without sacrificing candidate quality or experience

  • Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, with the ability to earn trust with candidates, hiring managers, and cross-functional partners

  • An experimental mindset and willingness to try new approaches to find, engage, and hire great talent

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience owning high-volume or seasonal hiring programs

  • Experience recruiting technical or engineering early-career talent

  • Experience supporting internship programs and intern-to-full-time conversion

  • Experience using AI throughout the recruiting workflow to improve sourcing, candidate engagement, and execution

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

About the Role

Ramp is seeking its first dedicated Financial Crimes Compliance Controls Senior Strategist to build and own the framework that demonstrates FCC controls are working as intended, remain effective as risk evolves, and can be clearly supported in bank-partner, audit, and regulatory examinations.

This is a senior individual-contributor role at the intersection of financial-crimes compliance, controls effectiveness, technology, data, and AI-enabled operations. You will own FCC’s approach to testing, documenting, and improving manual and automated controls, including procedures, detection rules, AI and LLM-enabled workflows, and automation deployments.

You will serve as FCC’s dedicated compliance partner for program-level Product, Engineering, Design, and Data (“PEDD”) initiatives, ensuring FCC requirements, controls, and risk considerations are incorporated into strategic product and technology planning. This role complements the broader team’s cross-functional partnerships by focusing specifically on major PEDD-led initiatives.

This is a builder role for an experienced financial-crimes compliance professional with deep analytical skills and strong BSA/AML, and sanctions subject-matter expertise You will assess emerging and existing financial-crimes risks, make sound and defensible control decisions, and help build the processes, technology partnerships, and governance needed for FCC to scale responsibly. You will not simply maintain existing processes. You will help shape how FCC’s controls environment, AI strategy, and product partnership model evolve.

What You’ll Do

  • Own FCC’s controls-effectiveness across manual procedures, detection rules, workflow controls, automation deployments, and AI or LLM-enabled capabilities.

  • Establish standards for testing, evidence retention, issue identification, remediation tracking, and ongoing control monitoring.

  • Serve as FCC’s dedicated compliance partner for major PEDD-led initiatives, defining FCC requirements and ensuring compliance needs are incorporated into product and technology planning.

  • Partner with PEDD to translate financial-crimes requirements into scalable workflows, controls, and user experiences.

  • Own FCC’s internal AI and automation strategy, including identifying high-value use cases and ensuring AI-enabled workflows are appropriately tested, documented, monitored, and supported by appropriate human oversight.

  • Use financial crimes domain expertise, data, and analytical methods to proactively evaluate risk coverage, identify emerging risks or control gaps, and drive solutions and improvements..

  • Serve as an independent, qualified secondary reviewer for FCC compliance reviews where segregation of duties or heightened review is required.

What You Need

  • 7+ years of experience in financial-crimes compliance, AML/BSA or sanctions.

  • At least 3 years of experience in a technical compliance, controls, compliance-testing, quality-assurance, or similar role.

  • At least 3 years of experience as an AML or financial-crimes trusted advisor, including partnering with technical, operational, product, or business stakeholders on risk-based controls and decisions.

  • Experience developing, implementing, or evaluating controls across both manual and technology-enabled processes.

  • Deep understanding of financial-crimes typologies and how risk evolves across products, payment flows, customer types, and operational processes.

  • AI fluency, including the ability to independently use approved AI tools, critically assess output quality and limitations, and lead strategic AI and automation initiatives within a compliance environment.

  • Strong data-analysis skills sufficient to assess control performance, evaluate AI or LLM-enabled controls, identify trends or gaps, and partner credibly with technical teams.

  • Experience presenting testing results, control documentation, risk findings, or program materials to regulators, examiners, auditors, or bank partners.

  • ACAMS certification or equivalent financial-crimes certification.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex compliance requirements and risk decisions clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Comfort operating with significant autonomy and building structure in a new, evolving role.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience evaluating or implementing AI, machine learning, LLM, automation, or decisioning controls in a regulated environment.

  • Experience supporting a fintech, payments, banking, card, or money-transmission compliance program.

  • Experience designing controls for transaction monitoring, KYC or KYB, EDD, sanctions screening, suspicious-activity reporting, or payment-risk workflows.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

At Ramp, people are the single biggest lever on our trajectory, and the bar for who joins this team gets higher every quarter, not lower. We are hiring our first dedicated Recruiter for GTM Expansion, based in London: someone who can map a market, identify the operators who will outperform their peers and run a full-cycle process that wins them.

The UK is the immediate mandate. You will partner with local and US-based leaders to turn an ambitious growth plan into a real commercial team, from first conversation through offer close. You will also help us build the recruiting approach, market knowledge and candidate networks that support Ramp's expansion into new GTM markets over time.

The recruiters who do this best combine craft on the front end, research, identification and calibration, with execution on the back end, closing, candidate experience and pipeline discipline. We are looking for both.

What You'll Do

• Own full-cycle recruiting for priority GTM Expansion hiring, starting with UK roles across Sales, Solutions Consulting, Partnerships and Customer Success.

• Build a sharp point of view on the UK market and future expansion markets: the companies producing strong talent, the people who outperform their peers and the communities that matter.

• Use research, data and AI as part of your everyday craft to identify and qualify exceptional candidates. We expect a written market point of view, not just a slate of profiles.

• Run thoughtful, personalised outreach grounded in the candidate's actual background, commercial motion or recent work. We care more about quality, replies and conversion than send volume.

• Partner with GTM leaders to turn ambitious hiring plans into a clear profile, credible process and realistic compensation strategy. Surface hard market truth early and push back constructively when needed.

• Own the candidate experience from first conversation through offer close: fast follow-up, clear communication, strong process discipline and a tailored closing plan for the candidates we most want.

• Build real presence for Ramp in London through the right relationships, referrals and targeted community activity. The point is pipeline and credibility, not events for their own sake.

• Work tightly with the wider GTM Recruiting team on calibration, sourcing support, insight and operating rhythm, while bringing strong local judgment.

• Help improve how Ramp recruits for expansion by capturing what works in the UK and applying it thoughtfully as we enter new markets.

What You Need

• 5+ years of full-cycle GTM or Sales recruiting experience, ideally in a high-growth technology company where quality and pace both mattered.

• Strong knowledge of the UK technology talent market and a credible local network, or clear evidence that you can build one quickly.

• A track record of finding and closing exceptional people, not simply running inherited processes. You can point to candidates you identified who became strong hires.

• Excellent sourcing and research instincts. You can explain why someone is genuinely differentiated, not only that they have the right title at the right company.

• Experience hiring across several GTM functions, such as AEs, Sales Leadership, Solutions Consulting, Partnerships, Customer Success or RevOps.

• Strong candidate-closing judgment. You listen closely, understand what each candidate is weighing and can build conviction against serious alternatives.

• The confidence to influence senior leaders, challenge a mis-scoped search and make a hiring process better without creating unnecessary friction.

• Comfort using data to understand funnel health, diagnose problems and hold an honest conversation about what needs to change.

• High ownership. You book the next step while you have the candidate, chase what is stuck and do not wait for a detailed brief to get useful work moving.

• Specific, sharp written communication. Your outreach and candidate updates should never feel template-driven.

Nice to Have

• Experience recruiting for a fintech, SaaS, infrastructure or similarly complex B2B product.

• Experience joining a company as the first recruiter in a new geography, or helping to scale an international business.

• Experience building an AI-augmented recruiting research workflow.

Why this Role

You will have unusual ownership over one of Ramp's most important growth priorities, with the support of an established Talent team rather than the isolation of a one-person recruiting function. The work is practical and high impact: build the UK commercial team, help leaders make better hiring decisions and raise the bar for how Ramp recruits as it enters new markets.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
